_doc: Why each gate item left in the pilot bake is there and which task owns it (P1-017, MAP_REPAIR.md 'Verification': the six gate counts are 0 or each item is explained in the report). tools/bake/report/gates.ts matches an entry to an item by its id (a strip end 'w<way>.<piece>_<n> start|end', a map edge node 'm<way>.<n>', a face pair 'a|b') or by its kind. An item no entry explains stops the bake before tiles are written (invariant GATES-01). Entries that match nothing in a bake are listed in health.json gateReport.idle: delete them once their owner fixed the item. findings lists known defects outside the six gates with their owners, copied into health.json gateReport.findings.

explanations.why: a junction lies within its own cut length (up to 18 m, the cluster rule) of the pilot stage outline, so the lane model takes the map edge node into the junction (or keeps a stub) instead of ending the road at the outline. The pilot outline is a stage edge inside the centre block, not a block or map edge: the next stage bake carries these roads on. The real map edge gets closures (gate, loop, barricade) when the whole block is baked.

explanations.owner: P1-036 follow-up (lane model: the Vikas Marg deck split east of ITO)
explanations.why: the lane model builds the Vikas Marg flyover east of ITO, where its two deck carriageways leave the ramp beside a slip road, as one junction 110 m long (jn838495928) whose arms reach from the ramp on fill to the deck ends, and a road at grade (w776652307.0_0) runs under its deck end. On the ground level the junction surface lies on that road and is cut back off the deck arm's mouth; on the deck level its other end sits on the ground (P1-036 tried it: the ground then ran into the slab, TERR-02). The fix is in the lane model: the deck arms need their own split zone, not a junction with the slip road.

explanations.owner: P1-036 follow-up (lane model: the Vikas Marg deck split east of ITO)
explanations.why: the same deck arm as the unjoined end: it ends 6.8 m up because the junction surface is cut back off its mouth where a road at grade passes under it.

explanations.owner: P1-036 follow-up (lane model at Kashmere Gate)
explanations.why: the Hanuman Mandir flyover ramp lies on fill beside a road at grade at Kashmere Gate (13.4 to 13.8 m2). The lane overlap check now counts it on the solved levels (health.json lanes.overlapSolved, P1-036), but only after the elevation step, so it is not handed back to the repair. Handing it back (tried in P1-036, one extra repair round on the solved levels) pushed the ramp across the road: the solve then failed (headroom 4.9 m over w292171521.1_0, 22 grades over their limit, no convergence). The fix belongs in the lane model of the Kashmere Gate cluster jn1863525196.

hairline overlaps of 0.02 to 0.03 m2 where a one-way link meets the road it joins at a shallow angle (a link onto Sikandra Road near Mandi House, a link into a merge zone in Old Delhi): the kerb rows of the two strips cross over a few centimetres. Over the 0.01 m2 pair limit, far under anything a player sees.

findings.what: junction clusters with no usable ring and oversize junction surfaces
findings.measured: 63 clusters with no usable ring (J2). P1-036 keeps each polygon set surface inside the hull of its arms' cut lines (6 m margin): the three widest went from 124,188, 60,078 and 34,530 m2 to 18,253, 14,038 and 5,985 m2. 10 surfaces are still over 3,000 m2, each listed with why in health.json mesh.oversize. Their lane paths still wander: about 57 km of the 133 km of J2 lane path runs off every road face, nearly all in jn1863525196 (Kashmere Gate), jn11840636119 and jn10255323278
